 Pittsburgh Steelers backup quarterback Mason Rudolph replaced Aaron Rodgers in the lopsided Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals. 
 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers will be in the Hall of Fame one day. On Sunday night, though, he looked every bit of 42 years old. And in arguably his worst game as a member of the Steelers, Rodgers didn’t finish the contest.
 Backup quarterback Mason Rudolph replaced Rodgers in the fourth quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals. At the time, the Bengals were leading 38-18.
 Rodgers finished the night 15 for 29 with 143 passing yards and two touchdowns. 
 This is the second time Rudolph replaced Rodgers due to a coach’s decision at the end of a game this season. It also happened in the 20-3 defeat to the New England Patriots in Week 2.
 Mason Rudolph Replaced Aaron Rodgers in Week 10 Loss
 The Steelers unloaded the bench late in Week 10 at Cincinnati. At running back, Lew Nichols received the final few carries, replacing Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.
 No. 3 tight end Robert Tonyan receive a target from Rudolph during what became the final drive of the contest.
 Rudolph was 1 for 3 with one passing yard after replacing Rodgers. The completion went to Nichols for one yard.
 One of Rudolph’s incompletions was originally ruled an interception linebacker Barrett Carter returned for a touchdown. Replay review, though, showed Carter didn’t catch the pass.
 Steelers’ Rodgers Struggles vs. Bengals
 Few, if any, Steelers players performed well Sunday night against Cincinnati. The Bengals outscored the Steelers 24-3 in the first half. Cincinnati added another touchdown to go ahead 31-3 before Pittsburgh reached the end zone for the first time.
 But Rodgers struggled significantly. He began the night 0 for 7. In the first half, he completed only 4 of 12 attempts for 25 yards.
 At one point in the third quarter, the Steelers offense had negative net passing yards.
 Rodgers also didn’t get much help. 
 The Pittsburgh wide receiver corps showcased why a lot of black and gold fans wanted the team to acquire a wideout at the NFL trade deadline Tuesday. The Steelers receivers didn’t have a single yard until the second half.
 The offensive line struggled to create rushing lanes against defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence and the Bengals defensive line. Cincinnati also registered three sacks against Rodgers.
 The Steelers defense put Rodgers and his unit in an early hole as well. Joe Burrow reached 300 yards before halftime and threw for at least three touchdowns for the fifth consecutive week.
 With the loss, the Steelers snapped their four-game winning streak and dropped to 6-3 this season. The defeat also moved the Steelers behind the Bengals in the AFC North standings.
 The Bengals have won five in a row and now sit 7-2 this season.
 Pittsburgh and Cincinnati split their 2026 season series. The Steelers defeated the Bengals 27-24 during their Week 3 showdown.
 After Sunday, Rodgers and the Steelers will have to regroup for their Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. While the Eagles have been one of the biggest disappointments around the league this season, the Steelers haven’t won in Philadelphia since 1965.
